reading_limit: New identity matched to the French-Revolution historian and BnF/Académie records. Argument support is the bounded original essay and Grunberg’s expressly named reading. His criticism targets a particular historical interpretation, not a personal causal influence or blanket theory classification.

relations.relationship: Challenges a specific Marxist/Jacobin historiography of the French Revolution for reproducing revolutionary and commemorative categories.
relations.evidence_note: Primary pp. 255–256 read. Furet’s polemical label and diagnosis remain his claims about a specific historiographical dispute, not a critique of every Marxist or a personal arrow to Marx.

relations.relationship: Examines political language and claims to represent the people as mechanisms of revolutionary power.
relations.evidence_note: Named reader Gérard Grunberg, pp. 895 and 897, on Penser. Full book unread; no universal acceptance, deterministic twentieth-century analogy or inference from institutional membership.
